newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen shares dip at noon on caution over bank.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares dip at noon on caution over bank.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices slid during the Tuesday morning session on selling prompted by caution over the temporary suspension of market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
The A share index dropped 8.33 points or 2.00 percent to 407.16 points on thin turnover of 2.3 billion yuan.
The B share index lost 1.80 points or 1.36 percent to 130.76 points on sluggish trade valued at HK$9.7 million.
"Investors cut holdings ahead of the bank's shareholders meeting," an analyst at Central-South Securities Co said.

Trading in the bank's A shares was suspended on Tuesday as the bank was due to hold a shareholders meeting to discuss its 1996 dividend plan, the Shenzhen bourse said. Trading would resume on Wednesday afternoon, it said.
Shenzhen Development Bank closed at 36.71 yuan on Monday.
The meeting would begin at 2.30 p.m. (0630 GMT) on Tuesday, a bank spokesman said.
The meeting was the morning's focal point because any change in the bank, China's only bank with a domestic listing, would have a significant impact on the overall market, brokers said.
Beijing last month ousted the bank's president He Yun as punishment for the bank having traded its own shares, and seized illegal profits of more than 90 million yuan.

Many investors were afraid the bank might use the meeting to announce a revision of its dividend plan, which consisted of a five-for-10 bonus issue plus a cash payment of 0.2 yuan per share, due to the cash seizure, brokers said.
"If the bank revises down the dividend, it is going to fall tomorrow and pull down the whole market," a stock analyst at Hainan Province Trust and Investment Co said.
Most brokers said they expected the dividend to remain intact because the bank did not calculate the illegal profits into its 1996 earnings.
"The seized money will affect the bank's 1997 earnings. The bank might reduce its bonus issue so as not to let its 1997 earnings be diluted too much," an analyst at Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Brokers said B shares would move in tandem with their A share counterparts in the near future.
In the B share market, Livzone Pharmaceutical put in the weakest performance, tumbling HK$0.25 or 6.28 percent to HK$3.73.

In the A share market, refrigerator maker Changsha Zhongyi was the biggest loser, falling 0.34 yuan or 5.92 percent to 5.40 yuan due to investor pessimism over the company's 1997 interim results, brokers said.
